correctness.rationale: Two explicit integer cut inequalities were checked exhaustively for all 128 cuts each; each extends to finite real ℓ1 by the cut cone representation. The cyclic certificate gives 42<=35c at n=7, and the path certificate gives 12<=10c in every n>=8. Exact rational averages of cyclic cuts give distance vectors (2,1) for n=5, (2,1,1) for n=6 and (2,6/5,6/5) for n=7. Full checker replay from the embedded script succeeded. The proof that every cycle-complement nonedge has distance two holds for all n>=5; the global extension is analytical.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family of dense vertex-transitive graphs has an exact non-isometric onset at seven vertices and a sharp uniform quantitative 20 percent embedding gap. Two explicit small local cut certificates govern all larger sizes, while a tight cyclic cut decomposition proves optimality at the boundary. This supplies a motivated invariant and robust obstruction without making unsupported claims for exact n>=8.
